speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Atony secondary to prolonged labor and macrosomia, complicated by urinary retention. The 11-pound infant suggests a large baby which increases the risk of incomplete uterine contraction, leading to the reported tenderness, fever, and decreased bowel sounds. I will now request a bedside pelvic exam and a bladder scan to confirm the findings.
